lines.en: And I don't know if they're a VIP or not. It actually doesn't matter. They are an entertainer.
lines.zh: 我不知道他們是不是 VIP，其實也沒關係。他們是娛樂者。

lines.en: I mean I was making everyone try every different kind.
lines.zh: 我是說，我讓每個人試各種不同的問題。

lines.en: I was using my students. They were trying them.
lines.zh: 我用我的學生，他們去試。

lines.en: I was seeing also I wanted to make sure they worked at work.
lines.zh: 我也在看，我想確定它們在職場上有用。

lines.en: They worked at home and they worked with kids, right? Right?
lines.zh: 在家裡有用，對小孩也有用，對吧？對吧？

lines.en: Like you can do a lot of the and you have to alter them slightly, but I want to make sure they work across the board.
lines.zh: 你可以用很多……你得稍微調整，但我想確定它們在各種情況都有用。

lines.en: And the sixth question is actually a signature question.
lines.zh: 第六個問題其實是一個招牌問題。

lines.en: So this is taking a step back and thinking, what do you love to talk about?
lines.zh: 這是退一步思考：你熱愛聊什麼？

lines.en: What do you love to talk about in conversation?
lines.zh: 你在對話中熱愛聊什麼？

lines.en: What do you love to talk about in conversation? When you're talking,
lines.zh: 你在對話中熱愛聊什麼？當你在說話時，

lines.en: what do I love to talk about? Yeah.
lines.zh: 我熱愛聊什麼？對。

lines.en: Not hear about necessarily, but talk about Oh gosh.
lines.zh: 不一定是聽，而是聊。天啊。

lines.en: We're going to reverse engineer it.
lines.zh: 我們要來逆向推導。

lines.en: This six question is about reverse engineering your love.
lines.zh: 這第六個問題是關於逆向推導你熱愛的東西。

lines.en: I like to talk about psychology, of people and stuff. Okay. Okay. So, great. Okay.
lines.zh: 我喜歡聊心理學，人之類的東西。好。好。很好。好。

lines.en: So, we you would want to reverse engineer questions about how and why.
lines.zh: 所以你會想逆向推導出關於「怎麼」和「為什麼」的問題。

lines.en: If you love psychology and behavior, you're going to want to ask someone why did you make that choice?
lines.zh: 如果你熱愛心理學和行為，你會想問別人：你為什麼做那個選擇？

lines.en: You know, what made you choose that path?
lines.zh: 你知道，是什麼讓你選擇那條路？

lines.en: You're going to want to ask more behavioral questions.
lines.zh: 你會想問更多行為方面的問題。

lines.en: Even in an interviewing perspective, let's talk about this for a second.
lines.zh: 就算從面試的角度，我們稍微聊一下這個。

lines.en: So, I believe in behavioral interviewing.
lines.zh: 我相信行為面試法。

lines.en: I believe in interview questions that actually let you know about someone's behavior, not just their opinions. Mhm.
lines.zh: 我相信面試問題應該讓你真正了解一個人的行為，而不只是他們的意見。嗯。

lines.en: So, for example, interviewers will make the mistake of asking, "What's your greatest weakness?"
lines.zh: 例如，面試官常犯的錯是問：「你最大的缺點是什麼？」

lines.en: It's not a good question because they're going to answer with a prepared answer.
lines.zh: 這不是個好問題，因為他們會用準備好的答案回答。

lines.en: It's not going to be real.
lines.zh: 那不會是真的。

lines.en: It's not going to tell you much.
lines.zh: 不會讓你了解太多。

lines.en: I would rather you ask, "What would your last manager say is your greatest weakness?"
lines.zh: 我寧願你問：「你上一任主管會說你最大的缺點是什麼？」

lines.en: That's a very different question.
lines.zh: 那是一個非常不同的問題。

lines.en: First of all, it's not going to be as practiced.
lines.zh: 首先，它不會那麼像背好的答案。

lines.en: Maybe after now it will be, but you're asking the person to step outside themselves from a behavior perspective.
lines.zh: 也許從現在起會了，但你是在請對方從行為的角度跳出自己。

lines.en: When we step outside of ourselves and think about someone else's opinion, we see different things even about ourselves and likely they're going to call your previous manager.
lines.zh: 當我們跳出自己、去想別人的意見時，我們甚至會看到關於自己的不同東西，而且他們很可能會打電話給你的前主管。

lines.en: Mhm. Right. So, they can confirm that in a in a phone call.
lines.zh: 嗯。對。所以他們可以在電話中確認。

lines.en: And you could even say, you know, when I call your previous manager, what would your previous manager say is your greatest weakness?
lines.zh: 你甚至可以說：你知道，當我打給你的前主管時，他會說你最大的缺點是什麼？

lines.en: You're going to get a juicy answer, right?
lines.zh: 你會得到一個很精彩的答案，對吧？

lines.en: And you can go verify it.
lines.zh: 而且你可以去查證。

lines.en: Another behavioral technique, which is why I like behavior so much, is not just asking, "Tell me about a recent time that you managed a project." Right?
lines.zh: 另一個行為技巧，這也是我這麼喜歡行為的原因，就是不要只問：「跟我說說你最近一次管理專案的經驗。」對吧？

lines.en: Right? We always ask for examples in interview.
lines.zh: 對吧？我們在面試中總會要求舉例。

lines.en: That's okay, but not great cuz they're going to pick the best one.
lines.zh: 那還可以，但不算好，因為他們會挑最好的那個。

lines.en: What you're better off saying is, tell me about the most recent time you managed a project.
lines.zh: 你最好說：跟我說說你「最近一次」管理專案的經驗。

lines.en: It should be in the last 3 months, 2 months, not a year or two ago.
lines.zh: 應該是最近三個月、兩個月內，不是一、兩年前。

lines.en: So asking for recency, asking for other people's opinions.
lines.zh: 所以要求最近的經驗、詢問別人的意見。

lines.en: The reason why I say this is because that would be crafting a type of answer that you want, trying to craft information about a previous experience that is real and not rehearsed.
lines.zh: 我會這樣說，是因為這是在設計你想要的那種答案，試著取得關於過去經驗、真實而非排練過的資訊。

lines.en: So for you, you'd be wanting to ask more behavior questions when you're at dinner, when you're here, obviously because that's what you love.
lines.zh: 所以對你來說，你在吃晚餐、在這裡的時候，你會想問更多行為方面的問題，顯然因為那是你熱愛的。

lines.en: Many successful people have signature questions.
lines.zh: 很多成功的人都有招牌問題。

lines.en: Like I know Amy Poehler at the end of her podcast, she always asks, "What are you laughing about?
lines.zh: 像我知道 Amy Poehler 在她的 podcast 結尾，總會問：「你最近在笑什麼？

lines.en: What's making you laugh recently?"
lines.zh: 最近什麼事讓你笑？」

lines.en: That's her signature question. example I use in the book is Ginny Yurich has a challenge a thousand hours outside
lines.zh: 那是她的招牌問題。我在書裡用的例子是 Ginny Yurich，她有一個「戶外一千小時」挑戰，

lines.en: which is spending a thousand hours with her kids outside playing more outside off of screens and she asks everyone her podcast what was your favorite outdoor memory
lines.zh: 就是花一千個小時和孩子在戶外玩，多在戶外、少看螢幕，她在 podcast 上會問每個人：你最喜歡的戶外回憶是什麼？

lines.en: because she loves talking about outdoors and and childhood nostalgia so the sixth question is inviting what do you love to talk about how can we engineer that in your conversations by looking for opportunities to bring it up
lines.zh: 因為她熱愛聊戶外和童年懷舊。所以第六個問題是在邀請：你熱愛聊什麼？我們可以怎麼透過找機會提起它，把它設計進你的對話裡？

lines.en: so at this stage I would turn to somebody when I when I feel like I've got that depth with them and I'd say what do you love to talk about and they might say do you know I really love talking about sports
lines.zh: 所以在這個階段，當我覺得和某人有了那種深度，我會轉向他說：你熱愛聊什麼？他們可能會說：你知道嗎，我真的很愛聊運動。

lines.en: and then are you saying that opens a door and gives me a clue as to how to connect with them so I future conversations with them should orientate towards sports or psychology or whatever their answer was
lines.zh: 你是說這會打開一扇門，給我一個如何和他們建立連結的線索，所以我之後和他們的對話應該以運動、心理學或他們的答案為主？

lines.en: no it would be you can ask what do you love to talk about it would be you Steven love to talk about behavior so you are going to ask more behavioral questions of them so you get to create your sixth question
lines.zh: 不是，是你可以問「你熱愛聊什麼」，而你，Steven，熱愛聊行為，所以你會問他們更多行為方面的問題，所以你是在創造你自己的第六個問題。

lines.en: right so like right now because I'm talking about conversation, my signature question is, "What's your favorite conversation starter?" Okay. Right.
lines.zh: 對，所以像現在因為我在談對話，我的招牌問題是：「你最喜歡的開場白是什麼？」好。對。

lines.zh: 我在研究《Cues》時，招牌問題是：「你認識最有魅力的人是誰？」嗯。

lines.zh: 或是你有沒有想過肢體語言？

lines.zh: 所以它可以依你的興趣而改變，但你是在為自己創造它。好。

lines.zh: 所以這是一個量身訂做的問題。
